title: Pinwheel motif — dense
subtitle: Solid double crochet fills the spaces between blades for a firm, thick pinwheel
excerpt: The dense pinwheel works dc stitches into the spaces between each blade section rather than leaving chain spaces open, giving a solid fabric with the same rotating blade outline but more body. This version blocks flat without pinning and is sturdy enough for pot holders and coasters.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 3 (1888), solid pinwheel chapter (Internet Archive).
heroPrompt: A dense pinwheel crochet motif in deep navy DK cotton on a pale linen background, photographed flat from above in soft daylight. Six solid blade sections visible with no open spaces between them, 12 cm across.

crochet.gaugeText: Finished dense pinwheel measures 12 cm across in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook.

chartDefinition.title: Pinwheel motif — dense
chartDefinition.caption: Treble blade sections alternate with dc-filled zones. No open chain spaces between blades.

glossaryTerms.definition: The double crochet stitches worked between each treble blade in a dense pinwheel, closing the space that would be a chain arch in a lacy version and giving the motif a solid fabric between the blades.

give the motif a solid fabric weight — the pinwheel outline remains visible from the blade height difference, but the piece has no holes.
Three rounds build a 12 cm hexagonal motif with six clear blade sections. It lies flat after a light steam without pinning. Use it as a coaster in cotton or a granny-bag panel in thicker yarn.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 12 g of DK-weight cotton. A 4 mm hook. Tapestry needle and scissors.

content.text: Magic ring. 12 dc into ring. Sl st to join. Pull to close. (12 dc.)
Ch 3 (counts as first tr). 2 tr into same st. 2 dc into next st. *3 tr into next st (blade). 2 dc into next st (fill zone).* Rep from * 4 more times. Sl st to top of beg ch-3. (18 tr, 12 dc.)

Ch 3 (counts as first tr). 3 tr into the NEXT blade of round 2 (offset one blade clockwise). 3 dc into the fill zone. *4 tr into next offset blade. 3 dc into fill zone.* Rep from * 4 more times. Sl st to top of beg ch-3. Fasten off. (24 tr, 18 dc.)
Work the block four-round for a solid circular motif without the blade construction. Or try the bavarian crochet square for a post-stitch ridge approach to building outward.
